children: Mining and transportation conglomerate Grupo Mexico

forecasts capital expenditures of $4 billion to $6 billion over the next three years for the main projects at its US unit Asarco, an executive said on Thursday, after the company reported a quarterly production decline on Tuesday.

Grupo Mexico's copper production in the third quarter reached 260,322 tons, down 1.9% from the same period a year ago, due to output decreases in Peru and at Asarco in the United States, the company said in its quarterly report, while the lower figures were partially offset by an increase in operations in Mexico.

The company's mining division chief Leonardo Contreras told analysts in a conference call on the third-quarter earnings results that the company is continuing its expansion of its Ray mine in Arizona, while carrying out feasibility studies.

He also said the company is "increasingly optimistic" about restarting the Hayden smelter and refinery in Arizona at a capacity of 1.4 million tons of copper concentrate per year to bring critical-mineral copper processing capacity back to the US.
"It would account for almost 350,000 metric tons of contained copper, and if that feeds into our refinery, we could be looking at 500,000 metric tons of copper. So we're optimistic", Contreras added.
Contreras said the Silver Bell project, also in Arizona, is undergoing feasibility studies as well, with more clarity expected in the coming quarters.
